A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoMind and MLE-Live. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the renumbered prompts and case study.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on 75 MLE-Bench competitions, eight ongoing Kaggle competitions, and 20 competitions used for ablations and analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluations on nine CoBench optimization tasks in Appendix F and Table 5.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same five-agent workflow, community representation, idea memory, and evaluation procedure. The CoBench experiment uses the previously defined variant without public resources; no new algorithmic component is introduced.

E1.justification: v3 adds nine CoBench combinatorial optimization tasks, including crew scheduling, graph colouring, bin packing, and TSP. This substantially extends coverage beyond Kaggle ML tasks to environments without notebooks, discussions, or leaderboard dynamics. Existing Kaggle coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The new CoBench comparison evaluates FunSearch and Greedy Refinement alongside AIDE. Neither additional comparator had reported evaluations in v2. This extends the comparator roster for the additional experiment; existing Kaggle and ablation comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces a distinct CoBench evaluation design: a shared gpt-5-mini backbone, 64 research steps, test-set feedback at each step, a 10-second execution limit, and normalized scores. These are settings for an added experiment; the existing Kaggle protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The resource-access ablations, task-category analysis, performance and code-complexity trajectories, Impostor Hunt error analysis, and denoising case study are retained. CoBench adds benchmark coverage and scores without a new ablation, sensitivity analysis, or controlled robustness comparison.

E5.justification: Table 4 retains identical mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting for token usage and cost, and the case-study seed information is unchanged. The added CoBench table reports point scores without new run-count, seed, or uncertainty information.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds a complete nine-task CoBench comparison. Average normalized scores are 0.887 for CoMind, 0.784 for AIDE, 0.834 for FunSearch, and 0.793 for Greedy Refinement; CoMind leads on four tasks. These substantially broaden the reported findings. Existing Kaggle scores and rankings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The community-state and dependency-graph definitions, idea-memory update, and evaluator mathematics in Section 4 are unchanged. The CoBench addition introduces no formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about MLE-Live, community-driven collaboration, and CoMind's performance. The headline 36% medal rate and 92.6% average human-competitor outperformance remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly frames performance in a community-free optimization environment as evidence concerning extensibility beyond Kaggle. The existing explanations of performance plateaus, runtime-related failures, and Impostor Hunt limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The CoBench addition documents its shared backbone, research-step budget, execution limit, feedback access, and resource restriction. Existing Kaggle hardware settings, hyperparameters, prompts, and case-study code are retained. No additional CoBench implementation or score-normalization details are supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Terminal-Bench, Inference Scaling Laws, and AI Impact on Human Proof Formalization Workflows, while removing the Xia et al. and OpenAI 2024 references. Other changes update publication metadata or consolidate duplicate SWE-Bench references; the central research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v3 adds short CoBench and LLM-use appendix sections, lightly revises the opening paragraph, and adds contact and conference-publication text. Appendix labels and cross-references change, but the main narrative and existing section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the CoBench results table and renumbers the previous Table 5 as Table 6. Appendix tables and figures are arranged more compactly, prompt formatting changes locally, and links gain colored styling. All nine existing figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: Appendix F and Table 5 provide empirical support for applicability beyond Kaggle, which v2 discussed only as a future direction. The shared-backbone comparison is useful, but covers nine selected tasks without community resources and supplies no uncertainty or score-normalization details. This modestly strengthens the paper's evidence while preserving its existing method and results.
